The Mitzvah · Sources

Three thousand years of instruction. One address.

From the Torah through the Talmud to the great halachic authorities, settling and acquiring the Land of Israel stands among the most cherished mitzvot.

Torah · Bamidbar 33:53

וְהוֹרַשְׁתֶּם אֶת הָאָרֶץ וִישַׁבְתֶּם בָּהּ כִּי לָכֶם נָתַתִּי אֶת הָאָרֶץ לָרֶשֶׁת אֹתָהּ

“You shall take possession of the land and settle in it, for I have given you the land to possess it.”

The Ramban counts this verse as one of the 613 commandments — binding in every generation (Additions to Sefer HaMitzvot, Positive Mitzvah 4).

Sifrei · Re'eh 80

יְשִׁיבַת אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל שְׁקוּלָה כְּנֶגֶד כָּל הַמִּצְווֹת שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה

“Dwelling in the Land of Israel is equal to all the mitzvot of the Torah.”

Talmud · Bava Kamma 80b · Gittin 8b

הַלּוֹקֵחַ בַּיִת בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל כּוֹתְבִין עָלָיו אוֹנוֹ אֲפִילּוּ בְּשַׁבָּת

So precious is buying a home in the Land that the Sages permitted arranging its deed even on Shabbat, through a non-Jew. Codified in Rambam, Shabbat 6:11 and Shulchan Aruch, Orach Chaim 306:11.

Talmud · Ketubot 110b · Rambam, Melachim 5:12

לְעוֹלָם יָדוּר אָדָם בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל

“A person should always dwell in the Land of Israel” — even in a city where most residents are not Jews, rather than outside it.

Tehillim 102:15 · Ketubot 112a

כִּי רָצוּ עֲבָדֶיךָ אֶת אֲבָנֶיהָ וְאֶת עֲפָרָהּ יְחֹנֵנוּ

“Your servants cherish her stones and favor her dust.” Rabbi Abba would kiss the stones of Akko upon arriving; Rabbi Chiya bar Gamda would roll in its dust.

Chatam Sofer · Sukkah 36a

הָעֲבוֹדָה בַּקַּרְקַע גּוּפָהּ מִצְוָה מִשּׁוּם יִשּׁוּב אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל

In the Land of Israel, even the everyday work of building and developing it is itself a mitzvah of settling the Land.

Igrot Moshe · Even HaEzer 1:102 · Pitchei Teshuva EH 75:6

A mitzvah one fulfills with every step taken.

Rav Moshe Feinstein of New York affirmed, with most authorities, that settling the Land is a Torah mitzvah — one fulfilled whenever a Jew chooses to take part in it.

The City · Netivot

בְּצֵל צִיּוּן הַבָּבָא סָאלִי זְכוּתוֹ יָגֵן עָלֵינוּ

Live in the shadow of the Baba Sali.

Netivot is home to the resting place of Rabbi Yisrael Abuhatzeira — the Baba Sali (1889–1984), the Moroccan-born tzaddik and kabbalist whose blessings are still sought by Jews the world over. Every day, visitors come to pray at his tomb. On his yahrzeit, the Hilula of 4 Shevat, tens of thousands fill the city.

Around the tziyun has grown a city of Torah: yeshivot, kollelim, batei knesset and a warm, traditional community — together with a modern train station, a new Hadassah medical center and fast-growing new neighborhoods.

The TziyunBaba Sali's tomb, minutes from home
By railDirect trains to Tel Aviv and Be'er Sheva
CommunityTorah institutions and Sephardic tradition

The City · Jerusalem

אִם אֶשְׁכָּחֵךְ יְרוּשָׁלָ͏ִם תִּשְׁכַּח יְמִינִי

Three times a day we pray for her. Now you can live in her.

For three thousand years, Jews have turned toward Jerusalem in every prayer, broken a glass at every wedding in her memory, and closed every Seder with “Next year in Jerusalem.” Her holiness, the Rambam teaches, was sanctified for its time and for all time to come — it never departed.

To hold a home within her walls of golden stone is to answer that prayer with your own address.

Nechemiah 11:2

וַיְבָרְכוּ הָעָם לְכֹל הָאֲנָשִׁים הַמִּתְנַדְּבִים לָשֶׁבֶת בִּירוּשָׁלָ͏ִם

“The people blessed all those who volunteered to dwell in Jerusalem.”

Mishnah · Ketubot 13:11

הַכֹּל מַעֲלִין לִירוּשָׁלַיִם וְאֵין הַכֹּל מוֹצִיאִין

Within the Land itself, Jerusalem stands highest: one may always move up to her, never away. Codified in Shulchan Aruch, Even HaEzer 75.

Tehillim 122:3

יְרוּשָׁלַ͏ִם הַבְּנוּיָה כְּעִיר שֶׁחֻבְּרָה לָּהּ יַחְדָּו

“Jerusalem, built up as a city joined together” — the city that binds all of Israel as one.

The City · Jaffa

וַאֲנַחְנוּ נִכְרֹת עֵצִים מִן הַלְּבָנוֹן… וּנְבִיאֵם לְךָ רַפְסֹדוֹת עַל יָם יָפוֹ

The ancient gateway to the Land. Your home by the Mediterranean.

Jaffa is woven into our story. The cedars for Shlomo's Holy Temple came ashore at the port of Yafo (Divrei HaYamim II 2:15), and again for the Second Temple in the days of Ezra (Ezra 3:7). From here the prophet Yonah set sail. For generations, it was the first shore that olim from across the world set foot upon.

Today Jaffa is part of Tel Aviv–Yafo, one of the most vibrant cities in the world: the sea promenade, the Old City's stone alleys and the flea market, galleries and restaurants — minutes from the business heart of Israel and a short drive from Ben Gurion Airport.

The City · Herzliya

אִם תִּרְצוּ אֵין זוֹ אַגָּדָה

The city that carries Herzl's name. The coast that carries Israel's future.

Founded in 1924 and named for Theodor Herzl, Herzliya is the living answer to his words: “If you will it, it is no legend.” A century later, it is one of Israel's most sought-after addresses.

Herzliya Pituach is home to the beaches, the marina and one of the country's leading high-tech districts, where global companies sit alongside Israeli start-ups. Green neighborhoods, excellent schools, warm communities and an easy ride to Tel Aviv make it a natural choice for families from abroad.

Beach & marinaLife on the Mediterranean
High-tech hubIsrael's innovation coast
Next to Tel AvivQuiet streets, city access

Questions, answered.

Can a US citizen register property in the Tabu?

Yes. Foreign residents can purchase and register apartments in Israel in their own name.

Do I need to travel to Israel?

No. The whole process can be completed by power of attorney, signed at an Israeli consulate or before a notary with apostille.

What does management include, and what does it cost?

Tenant placement, rent collection, arnona and utilities, maintenance and owner reporting. Fee: one month's rent per year.

What taxes apply to a foreign buyer?

Israeli purchase tax (Mas Rechisha) applies at the rates set for buyers who are not Israeli residents.
